conventions.positive-golden: tests/conformance/<edition>/<name>.cob + <name>.out; the directory selects --std. First line a comment `*> ISO §<clause> <rule> — <what is exercised>`. Unique PROGRAM-ID per program (a stale same-named assembly is served otherwise). Deterministic output only. Do NOT edit any manifest.json — return the entry; the director registers it.
conventions.negative-golden: tests/conformance/negative/<name>.cob + <name>.err (the expected diagnostic substring, e.g. COBOLNET1560). FIRST line of the .cob MUST be `*> reject-at: <year> [<year> ...]`. Do NOT edit the negative manifest — return the entry.
conventions.test-ref-forms: conformance:<edition>/<case> (positive, spec-derived) · conformance:negative/<case> · unit:<Class>.<Method> · conformance-test:<Class>.<Method>. nist:/characterization: and any *_MatchesLegacy method are NOT spec-derived and cannot close a row.
conventions.compiler: src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe <file.cob> --std <85|2002|2014|2023> --run  (run in a scratch dir; never dotnet build/test — the tree is shared and a guard refuses builds while a fleet is live).
conventions.citation-check: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check <clause> "<quoted text>"  — every § you cite, no exceptions.

rows.subject: UNSTRING statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: "The data item referenced by identifier-4 is the receiving operand for data. The data item referenced by identifier-5 is the receiving operand for delimiters." (cite.py --check 14.9.48.3 OK). Code: BindUnstring resolves identifier-4 (drefs[0]) and identifier-5 (DELIMITER IN) through host.Expr.ResolveReceiving — the receiving chokepoint — and binds each store as a MOVE into it (ImplicitMovePhrase.UnstringInto / UnstringDelimiterIn). Probes: a constant-name as DELIMITER IN (u9const.cob) -> COBOLNET1548 (§13.10.4 GR1); a function-identifier as INTO (u9func.cob) and a literal as INTO (u9lit.cob) are refused at parse; DELIMITER IN receives the matched delimiter (ufmtrev.cob B=[,   ]). No spec-derived test pins the receiving designation for UNSTRING INTO/DELIMITER IN specifically (pb429_page_counter_receiving covers identifier-7, a different operand), so test-ref is empty.
rows.rule-text: The data item referenced by identifier-4 is the receiving operand for data. The data item referenced by identifier-5 is the receiving operand for delimiters.

rows.subject: UNSTRING statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: GR1 'All references to identifier-2 and literal-1 apply equally to identifier-3 and literal-2' (cite.py --check 14.9.48.4 'apply equally to identifier-3 and literal-2' -> OK 14.9.48.4 1)). The binder folds every DELIMITED BY / OR item through ONE loop (dp.unstringDelimiterItem()) into one List<BoundUnstringDelimiter>; the emitter renders one string[]/bool[] pair and the kernel treats every index alike (GR9 zero-length skip, GR7 ALL flag, GR10 scan). No code distinguishes the first delimiter from the OR'd ones, so every rule over identifier-2/literal-1 applies to identifier-3/literal-2 by construction. Probe p2 T1/T2/T3 exercised OR'd literals with ALL on the second position: correct. No spec-derived test names this rule.
rows.rule-text: All references to identifier-2 and literal-1 apply equally to identifier-3 and literal-2, respectively, and all recursions thereof.

rows.subject: UNSTRING statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: GR6 'incremented by 1 for each occurrence of the data item referenced by identifier-4 accessed during the UNSTRING operation' (cite.py --check -> OK 14.9.48.4 6)). EmitUnstring '{tly} += 1' once per receiver whose UnstringExtract returned >= 0 (acted upon), none for a receiver skipped on sender exhaustion. Probe p2 T3 (3 receivers) 5 -> 08; p1 GR9A 0 -> 03, GR9B 0 -> 02. Only legacy-differential tests cover it -> test-ref empty. Companion of GR14.
rows.rule-text: The data item referenced by identifier-8 is a counter that is incremented by 1 for each occurrence of the data item referenced by identifier-4 accessed during the UNSTRING operation.

rows.subject: UNSTRING statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: GR9 four sentences (cite.py --check -> OK 14.9.48.4 9)). (1) each operand one delimiter - one array entry each. (2) multi-character delimiter only contiguous and in order - IndexOf(del, pos, Ordinal); probe p2 T2 "AB" matched only at 'AB'. (3) 'If the data item referenced by identifier-2 or identifier-3 is a zero-length item, that delimiter is ignored' - kernel 'if (del.Length == 0) continue'; probe p1 GR9A DELIMITED BY WS-Z (dynamic-length, "") OR "," over 'AB,,CD;EF' -> [AB  ][    ][CD;E] P=10 T=03 (the "," delimiter alone). (4) all identifiers zero-length and no literal -> as if DELIMITED absent: kernel anyDelim=false uses receiverSize, and the emitter supplies the real size (sizeCanGovern when every delimiter is a field/computed operand); probe p1 GR9B DELIMITED BY WS-Z INTO A1 A2 -> [AB,,][CD;E] P=09 + OVF (F unexamined), exactly the no-DELIMITED result. No spec-derived test pins sentences 3/4 -> test-ref empty. [editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the two zero-length sentences are 2014+: zero-length items are post-2002)]
rows.rule-text: Each literal-1 or the data item referenced by identifier-2 represents one delimiter. When a delimiter contains two or more characters, all of the characters shall be present in contiguous positions of the sending item, and in the order given, to be recognized as a delimiter. If the data item referenced by identifier-2 or identifier-3 is a zero-length item, that delimiter is ignored. When neither literal-1 nor literal-2 is specified and all data items referenced by identifier-2 and identifier-3 are zero-length items, it is as if the DELIMITED phrase were not specified.

rows.subject: UNSTRING statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: GR10: OR condition; 'No character(s) in the sending field shall be considered a part of more than one delimiter' and 'Each delimiter is applied to the sending field in the sequence specified' (cite.py --check 14.9.48.4 -> OK 10)). Kernel: for each non-empty delimiter IndexOf(del, pos); the earliest position wins, a same-position tie keeps the first listed (strict <); the matched characters are consumed once (pointer = pos+extractLen+consumed+1), so no character belongs to two delimiters. Probe p2 over 'XABYAAAZ,,Q ': DELIMITED BY "A" OR "AB" -> A1 [X] D1 [A] C1 01, A2 [BY] D2 [A] C2 02; DELIMITED BY "AB" OR "A" -> [X][AB]01 [Y][A]01 - both the spec-derived values. Existing StringUnstringDifferentialTests.Unstring_OrDelimiters_EarliestWins_TieGoesToFirstListed is AssertSameAsLegacy (legacy differential) so it does NOT close the row; test-ref empty.
rows.rule-text: When two or more delimiters are specified in the DELIMITED BY phrase, an OR condition exists between them. Each delimiter is compared to the sending field. If a match occurs, the character(s) in the sending field is considered to be a single delimiter. No character(s) in the sending field shall be considered a part of more than one delimiter. Each delimiter is applied to the sending field in the sequence specified in the UNSTRING statement.

rows.subject: UNSTRING statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: GR14 'value at the beginning of the execution of the statement plus a value equal to the number of identifier-4 receiving data items accessed' (cite.py --check -> OK 14.9.48.4 14)). EmitUnstring: tly initialized from the TALLYING item's current value, += 1 inside the 'if (cnt >= 0)' acted-upon block only (a receiver skipped because the sender was exhausted, GR11g, is not accessed), stored back after the loop. Probe p2 T3: 5 + 3 receivers = 08; p2 T4 (GR15a overflow): 0 -> 00 (no receiver accessed). The only covering test (StringUnstringDifferentialTests.Unstring_DelimiterIn_CountIn_TallyingAddsToCurrentValue) is legacy-differential -> test-ref empty.
rows.rule-text: When the execution of an UNSTRING statement with a TALLYING phrase is completed, the content of the data item referenced by identifier-8 contains a value equal to its value at the beginning of the execution of the statement plus a value equal to the number of identifier-4 receiving data items accessed during execution of the statement.

rows.subject: UNSTRING statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: GR17 'the ON OVERFLOW phrase, if specified, is ignored and control is transferred to the end of the UNSTRING statement or, if the NOT ON OVERFLOW phrase is specified, to imperative-statement-2' (cite.py --check -> OK 14.9.48.4 17)). EmitOverflow: 'if (!flag)' runs the NOT list; the ON list only under 'if (flag)'; pointer/tally are stored before the dispatch (so imperative-statement-2 sees the completed values). Probe p2 T6 (P=12, one char examined, no overflow) -> 'T6 NOVF'. The UNSTRING NOT-ON path is pinned only by the legacy-differential Unstring_SourceExhausted_IsNotOverflow_RemainingReceiversUntouched; phrase_order_overflow pins NOT-ON only for STRING -> test-ref empty.
rows.rule-text: If, at the time of execution of an UNSTRING statement, the conditions described in General rule 15 are not encountered, after completion of the transfer of data according to the other general rules, the ON OVERFLOW phrase, if specified, is ignored and control is transferred to the end of the UNSTRING statement or, if the NOT ON OVERFLOW phrase is specified, to imperative-statement-2. If control is returned from imperative-statement-2, control is then transferred to the end of the UNSTRING statement.

rows.subject: UNSTRING statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: GR18: overlapping identifier-1..-8 -> 'the result of the execution of this statement is undefined' (cite.py --check -> OK 14.9.48.4 18)). The rule imposes no requirement on the implementation; EmitUnstring reads the sender image and every delimiter value ONCE at initiation and the pointer/tally into locals, so any overlap yields a deterministic (undefined-by-spec) result and no crash. Nothing to test.
rows.rule-text: If identifier-1, identifier-2, or identifier-3, occupies the same storage area as identifier-4, identifier-5, identifier-6, identifier-7, or identifier-8, or if identifier-4, identifier-5, or identifier-6, occupies the same storage area as identifier-7 or identifier-8, or if identifier-7 and identifier-8 occupy the same storage area, the result of the execution of this statement is undefined, even if they are defined by the same data description entry. (See 14.6.10, Overlapping operands.)
